assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: partial
daemon_capability: n/a; driver_capability: n/a

The dialog CLASS exists in opencode's model but no INSTANCE of it is reachable on any path opencode can be driven on here. Frozen, and not because irrlicht cannot see it — if one arose, the daemon would.

## What opencode blocks on, enumerated rather than sampled

opencode has exactly one blocking-dialog mechanism: `Permission.ask`. Everything that stops a session and waits for the user goes through it, so the question "does opencode raise a blocking dialog attached to no tool call?" reduces to "is there a `Permission.ask` call site with no tool call in flight?" — which is enumerable. The request type itself makes clear the product models both shapes (verbatim from the 1.14.50 bundle):

    class PermissionRequest {
      id, sessionID, permission, patterns, metadata, always,
      tool: optional({ messageID, callID })      // <- OPTIONAL
    }

Every `Permission.ask` call site in the bundle, and whether a tool call is open when it fires:

| call site | tool in flight? |
|---|---|
| read / glob / grep / list / lsp / webfetch / websearch / repo_overview / repo_clone / skill / todowrite / task / edit / write / patch / bash | YES — each is inside that tool's own `execute`, and the tool-context wrapper injects `tool:{messageID,callID}` into the ask |
| every MCP server tool (`so.ask({permission:go,…})` in the generic tool wrapper) | YES — same wrapper, same injection |
| `external_directory` (`Tool.assertExternalDirectory`, and `ShellTool.ask`'s dirs branch) | YES — called from read/glob/grep/write/edit/lsp/repo_overview and from bash |
| `doom_loop` | YES — see below |
| `workflow_tool_approval` | **NO** — see below |

## The four triggers this row names, each checked

**1. Sandbox or network-access confirmation — absent.** opencode's gateable permission keys are exhaustively listed by its own `PermissionConfig` schema and repeated verbatim in its config-help prose: `read, edit, glob, grep, list, bash, task, external_directory, todowrite, question, webfetch, websearch, repo_clone, repo_overview, lsp, doom_loop, skill`. There is no sandbox or network-egress key. The two nearest analogues are network gates that ARE tool calls (`webfetch`, `websearch`) and a filesystem-scope gate (`external_directory`) raised from inside a tool's execute. opencode does have a `workspace.type.sandbox` concept, but it is a workspace KIND in the settings UI, not a per-session confirmation dialog.

**2. First-use trust prompt for a workspace or a server — absent.** Every occurrence of `trust`/`Trust` in the 106 MB bundle (251 hits, all inspected by context) belongs to bun's `trustedDependencies` installer text, TLS/OCSP trust-chain handling, sigstore TUF's `trustedSet`, or an embedded emacs epg regexp table. opencode has no workspace-trust or server-trust gate — unlike codex, whose folder-trust prompt its own cells have to answer at boot.

**3. Server-driven MCP elicitation — structurally unavailable.** opencode builds its MCP client as `new Py({name:"opencode", version:$D})` — clientInfo only, no options and therefore no `capabilities`. The bundled MCP SDK gates elicitation on the client having declared it: `assertRequestHandlerCapability` throws ``Client does not support elicitation capability (required for elicitation/create)``, and `setRequestHandler` for `elicitation/create` additionally rejects both modes unless `supportsFormMode`/`supportsUrlMode` are set. There is no `setRequestHandler`, no `registerCapabilities` and no `elicitation` string anywhere in opencode's own MCP module — every `elicitation` occurrence in the binary is SDK schema or ACP protocol definition, never a declaration or a handler. A server cannot elicit from opencode.

**4. Auto-mode or settings review — present in form, but a tool IS in flight.** `doom_loop` is a genuine product-raised review: opencode ships it as a permission key, its UI copy is `Continue after repeated failures` / `This keeps the session running despite repeated failures`, and the default `build` agent ships it as `doom_loop: "ask"`. It is the closest thing opencode has to this row. It fails the row's second acceptance criterion, on source rather than on inference. It is raised from the `case "tool-call"` stream-part handler, and the line immediately before it sets the tool part to running:

    yield*F(b.toolCallId,(no)=>({…no, tool:b.toolName,
        state:{…no.state, status:"running", input:b.input, time:{start:Date.now()}}}));
    let T = ao.parts(g.assistantMessage.id).slice(-lb);
    if (T.length!==lb || !T.every(no => no.type==="tool" && no.tool===b.toolName && …)) return;
    yield* w.ask({permission:"doom_loop", patterns:[b.toolName], sessionID:…,
                  metadata:{tool:b.toolName, input:b.input}, always:[b.toolName], …});

So while the doom_loop modal is held there IS an open tool call in the store, at `state.status="running"`. An integration deriving its signals from an open tool window would not MISS this episode — which is precisely the failure mode this row exists to expose. Recording it would produce a green that asserts the wrong thing. (It is also not mechanically elicitable: it requires the model to emit the SAME tool call with byte-identical input N times consecutively.)

## The one genuine instance, and why it is still frozen

`workflow_tool_approval` IS tool-less. It is raised by an `approvalHandler` that receives a BATCH of pending tool calls and asks once, before any of them starts, with no `tool:` field on the request:

    b.approvalHandler = N.bind(async (T) => { …
      await Q.promise(n.ask({id:no, sessionID:…, permission:"workflow_tool_approval",
                             patterns:a, metadata:{tools:T}, always:a, ruleset:[]})); … })

It is installed only under `if (c instanceof zf)`, where that class carries `workflowOptions`, `sessionWorkflows`, `currentWorkflowId` and `approveAndResume` — opencode's workflow-provider model, the path its GitLab Agent Platform provider (`family:"gitlab-ai-provider"`, `options:{workflowRef}`, models named `Agent Platform (…)`) drives. This host is configured for a local LM Studio model and two OpenAI-compatible providers; it has no workflow-provider account, and none of the four triggers this row names is what that dialog is. That is why the verdict is `partial` rather than `yes` — and why it is `partial` rather than `no`: claiming opencode cannot raise a tool-less dialog at all would be false, and a future assessor would have to re-derive the whole enumeration to find out.

## Why daemon is `n/a` and NOT `incapable`

This is the distinction that decides how the cell is read later. `incapable` would claim irrlicht could not observe such a dialog. It could. `workflow_tool_approval` and `doom_loop` both go through the same `Permission.ask`, which publishes the same `permission.asked` bus event carrying the same `sessionID`; irrlicht's plugin forwards it, `HandlePermissionPromptHook` holds `SignalPermissionPrompt`, and `state_classifier` rule 0 (`m.PermissionPending` — a bare bool, with no tool dimension) turns it into `waiting`. `permission.replied` carries the release, on approve AND on reject. Both edges the row asserts would land. The pillar is `n/a` because the behaviour does not arise on any drivable path, not because the daemon would miss it.

## What would unblock this cell

Either (a) opencode declares an `elicitation` client capability on its MCP client and renders a server elicitation as a blocking dialog — one constructor argument upstream, and the SDK plumbing is already vendored; or (b) a workflow-capable provider (GitLab Agent Platform) is configured on the recording host, making `workflow_tool_approval` reachable. Re-assess if either changes. Nothing on irrlicht's side is blocking.

## Confidence

0.8. The enumeration is read directly out of the installed binary (`PermissionConfig`'s key list, the `PermissionRequest` class with its optional `tool`, every `Permission.ask` call site, the doom_loop handler in full, the workflow approvalHandler and its `instanceof` guard, the MCP client construction, the SDK's elicitation capability assertions), and the daemon half directly out of the adapter and classifier source. Not higher because the negative claims rest on an exhaustive static read of a minified bundle rather than on driving opencode and watching no dialog appear — and because `zf`'s provider binding is inferred from the class's own workflow fields plus opencode's shipped GitLab provider rather than from a line that names them together.
caveats: `daemon: n/a` here means 'the pillar does not apply', NOT 'irrlicht cannot see it'. If a tool-less opencode dialog did arise, the hook channel (#1719/epic #1355) would carry BOTH edges: permission.asked -> HandlePermissionPromptHook -> SignalPermissionPrompt -> state_classifier rule 0 -> waiting, and permission.replied -> ReleasePermissionPromptHold -> out of waiting (published for reject as well as once/always). Do not read this cell as evidence of an observability gap.

doom_loop is the near-miss and must not be substituted for this row. It is a real product-raised review ('Continue after repeated failures'), it is shipped as `doom_loop: "ask"` in the default build agent, and its permission request carries no `tool:` field — but it is raised from the `case "tool-call"` stream handler on the line AFTER the tool part is set to state.status="running", so a tool call IS in flight while the modal is held. That fails this row's acceptance criterion #2 verbatim, and a recording of it would be a green asserting the wrong thing. It is also not mechanically elicitable (it needs N consecutive byte-identical tool calls from the model).

workflow_tool_approval is the one genuinely tool-less dialog and is PROVIDER-GATED: installed only under `if (c instanceof zf)`, the workflow-provider model class (workflowOptions / sessionWorkflows / currentWorkflowId / approveAndResume), which opencode's GitLab Agent Platform provider drives. This host has no such account (~/.config/opencode/opencode.json configures lmstudio + ionos + the built-in providers). The zf-to-GitLab binding is INFERRED from the class's workflow fields plus opencode's shipped gitlab-ai-provider models named 'Agent Platform (…)' with options:{workflowRef}; no single line names them together.

MCP elicitation is unavailable by construction, not by configuration: opencode builds its client as `new Py({name:"opencode",version:$D})` with no capabilities argument, and the vendored SDK throws 'Client does not support elicitation capability' for elicitation/create. Adding a server with elicitation support to this host would NOT make the cell recordable.

The negative claims for triggers 1 and 2 rest on an exhaustive static read of a minified 106 MB bun bundle: the PermissionConfig key list (which has no sandbox/network/trust key) and a context inspection of all 251 trust/Trust occurrences (bun trustedDependencies, TLS/OCSP, sigstore TUF, an emacs epg table — none an opencode dialog). A live TUI probe was NOT run; this verb spends no model calls. A probe could only confirm an absence the schema already forecloses, but say so rather than imply otherwise.

If this cell is ever re-opened, re-check the permission key list first: it is the cheapest possible signal that opencode grew a new blocking-dialog class, and it is printed verbatim in the binary in two places (the PermissionConfig schema and opencode's own config-help prose).

`assertRequestHandlerCapability`: case "elicitation/create" throws `Client does not support elicitation capability (required for ...)` when _capabilities.elicitation is unset; the elicitation/create setRequestHandler wrapper further throws 'Client does not support form-mode elicitation requests' / '...URL-mode...' unless supportsFormMode/supportsUrlMode. opencode declares neither and registers no handler, so trigger 3 is structurally unavailable.

The payload is {hook_event_name, session_id} with no tool field, so a tool-less dialog would be observed exactly like a tool-carried one — both edges would land if the behaviour arose.
rule 0 (lines 106-118): when = m.PermissionPending, a bare bool with no tool dimension. Nothing on the opencode path requires an open tool call to reach waiting.

the sibling assessed in the same pass, which establishes the hook channel end-to-end (agent yes / daemon full / driver ready). It is what makes this cell's `n/a` a statement about opencode's dialog inventory rather than about irrlicht's observability.

precedent for this cell's shape: opencode ships a plan MODE but not the plan-APPROVAL primitive that row asserts, recorded as agent_supports:partial with the recipe applicable:false. Same 'capability present in the wrong form' verdict.

recipe.notes: FROZEN at assessment — agent_supports:partial, daemon_capability:n/a, driver_capability:n/a. No recording, no phases. opencode's ONLY blocking-dialog mechanism is Permission.ask, and every call site of it except two is inside a tool's execute with `tool:{messageID,callID}` injected by the tool-context wrapper. Of the two exceptions: doom_loop ('Continue after repeated failures', shipped as doom_loop:"ask" in the default build agent) is raised from the `case "tool-call"` stream handler on the line AFTER the tool part is written at state.status="running", so a tool call IS in flight while the modal is held — it fails this row's acceptance criterion #2 and recording it would assert the wrong thing; workflow_tool_approval IS genuinely tool-less (a batch approval asked once before any of the pending calls starts, with no tool field) but is installed only under `if (c instanceof zf)`, the workflow-provider model class opencode's GitLab Agent Platform provider drives, for which this host has no account. NONE of the four triggers the scenario names exists on a drivable path: no sandbox/network permission key exists in PermissionConfig; no workspace- or server-trust prompt exists anywhere in the bundle (all 251 trust/Trust hits are bun/TLS/sigstore/emacs); MCP elicitation is foreclosed because opencode constructs its MCP client with no capabilities argument and the vendored SDK throws 'Client does not support elicitation capability'; and the auto-mode/settings-review slot is filled by doom_loop, which has an open tool call. DO NOT substitute a tool-permission dialog — that behaviour is tool-gate-permission-prompt (2.19) and permission-gate-non-mutating-tool (2.26), the latter assessed record in this same pass. UNBLOCK: either opencode declares an elicitation client capability on its MCP client (one constructor argument upstream; the SDK plumbing is already vendored), or a workflow-capable provider is configured on the recording host. Nothing on irrlicht's side blocks this: if such a dialog arose, permission.asked/permission.replied would carry both edges through the hook channel (#1719/epic #1355) and state_classifier rule 0 would render it as waiting — which is why daemon_capability is n/a (the pillar does not apply) and NOT incapable (the daemon would see it).
